headlines.title: Blue Angels set to practice ahead of San Francisco Fleet Week air shows
headlines.description: The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are expected to take to the skies Thursday for a practice session ahead of three straight days of San Francisco Fleet Week air shows. People in San Francisco, specifically the north side of the city, will likely hear and spot the fighter jets buzzing the area. Fleet Week air shows, headlined by the Blue Angels, are scheduled to take place on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. The Blue Angels are known for extreme aerobatics precision, flying as close as about 18 inches apart while reaching speeds of up to 700 mph. Blue Angels officers and enlisted team members will hold jet-side interviews at Oakland’s airport before Thursday’s practice. The Blue Angels did not perform during last year’s Fleet Week due to the federal government shutdown. headlines.title: Man charged following crash that killed 2 in Daly City
headlines.description: A 28-year-old San Francisco man is accused of running a red light and crashing into another vehicle in Daly City last weekend, killing two people, San Mateo County prosecutors said Thursday. Alvaro Caballero Arteaga made his initial appearance in court Wednesday to face charges for a crash reported on Sunday at the intersection of San Jose Avenue and Flournoy Street, according to the San Mateo County District Attorney’s Office. Caballero Arteaga allegedly sped through a red light and broadsided another vehicle, killing the driver Rhiannon Lawler and passenger Agustin Garcia, prosecutors said. A preliminary alcohol screening showed he had a blood alcohol level of 0.15%, and investigators learned his driver’s license had been suspended following an arrest in February in Alameda County for misdemeanor drunk driving, according to the district attorney’s office. Caballero Arteaga did not enter a plea at his arraignment Wednesday and was assigned an attorney via the county’s Private Defender Program. He will return to court on Oct. 15 for further arraignment and remains in custody on “no bail” status, prosecutors said.

headlines.title: Driver dies, 2 passengers hospitalized after San Jose crash
headlines.description: A motorist died in a solo vehicle crash in San Jose early Thursday morning, according to police. Just before 3:30 a.m., officers were alerted to a report of a crash that occurred in the area of Zanker Road and Daggett Drive. “The driver ultimately succumbed to their injuries and was pronounced deceased at the scene,” the San Jose Police Department said on social media. Two passengers were also sent to a hospital with major injuries and have since stabilized, police said. Based on the preliminary investigation, the vehicle crashed into a concrete wall in the center median of Zanker Road. Police advised motorists to avoid the area and use alternate routes while road closures are in place at the scene of the crash.

headlines.title: Microsoft being suspended from program to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers, Vance says
headlines.description: President Donald Trump’s administration is suspending tech giant Microsoft from a program to apply for green cards for workers who come to the U.S. to live and work using an H-1B visa as it accuses the company of fraud. “If you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” said Vice President JD Vance in a White House news conference announcing the decision. The H-1B program has long been a target of Trump supporters who say that the program undercuts American workers and is rife with abuse. H-1B visas are meant for high-skilled jobs that are difficult to find American workers to fill. Technology companies are the biggest users, with nearly three-quarters of approvals going to workers from India. Microsoft, which is based in Redmond, Washington, near Seattle, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Vance announcement came one day after Trump’s Republican administration launched another broadside against international students and their ability to work in the U.S. The Department of Homeland Security on Wednesday proposed a $70,000 fee for international students seeking to work in the United States. The proposed rule would require schools to pay the fee for every student who participates in the Optional Practical Training program, known as OPT, which allows students to work in jobs related to their major during or after their time in school. Vance also called out universities that he suggested were abusing a program to allow international students to come to the U.S. These temporary visas, called J-1 visas, allow international visitors to temporarily come to the U.S. for work and study exchange programs. Vance singled out nine universities that he said merited further investigation for J-1 visa fraud, saying they used the program in greater proportions than their counterparts.

headlines.title: 2 severely injured in suspected hit-and-run collision in Berkeley
headlines.description: Two people in their 70s were severely injured in a suspected hit-and-run collision at a Berkeley intersection Wednesday night, according to police. Around 9 p.m., officers were alerted to a report that two pedestrians were struck by a vehicle at the intersection of University Avenue and Eighth Street. When they arrived, the officers found a 78-year-old man and a 75-year-old woman with serious injuries. The driver who struck the pedestrians was nowhere to be found, the Berkeley Police Department said. Berkeley Fire Department crews sent both victims to a hospital. “Due to the severity of the collision, the Department’s Fatal Accident Investigation Team is conducting the investigation. Preliminary information indicates that the man and woman were crossing University Avenue in the eastern crosswalk when they were struck by a dark-colored sedan traveling eastbound on University Avenue,” police said. Anyone with information about this case is asked to contact the department’s traffic unit at 510-981-5980.

headlines.title: Candidates debate key issues in California's 14th Congressional District race
headlines.description: Rep. Aisha Wahab and BART Board President Melissa Hernandez faced off Wednesday night in a debate for California’s 14th Congressional District. The debate, put on by the Dublin Chamber of Commerce, addressed a number of issues voters will consider when they cast their ballots in November. Wahab won the race earlier this year to finish Eric Swalwell’s term after he resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct, becoming the first Afghan American elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. Wahab and Hernandez are now competing for the seat for the new term that begins in January. During the debate, the candidates were asked about immigration, health care, housing affordability and whether the federal government should regulate the development of AI data centers. “Our utilities companies are not going to prioritize the infrastructure improvements that they need to do, which is something that we have been having challenges with,” Wahab said. “And AI is the literal industrial revolution to all industries that we are talking about. And I think that there is a balancing act that we need to ensure when we are talking about a roadmap for both AI and data centers.” Hernandez also addressed federal regulation of AI. “Right now, you have different states doing different structures and boundaries and so on, but it definitely needs to be at the federal level and not have all this different type of patchwork,” Hernandez said. “And the reason why I say that is because it needs to be universal.” According to the East Bay Times, Hernandez criticized Wahab for remarks she made about wanting to have a relationship with the leaders of Afghanistan, which is currently under the control of the Taliban. Wahab criticized Hernandez for receiving campaign contributions from AIPAC, which supports American-Israeli interests. Early voting started Monday in Alameda County and throughout the rest of the state. Mail-in ballots have also been sent to voters and should be arriving at homes soon, if they haven’t already. Election Day is Nov. 3.

headlines.title: Some guardrails on ChatGPT for Teens don't work as promised, watchdog group says
headlines.description: Some of the guardrails that OpenAI included in its ChatGPT for Teens product don’t work as intended and the chatbot poses an “unacceptable risk” to children, according to a report Wednesday by Common Sense Media. The watchdog group urged OpenAI to restrict the chatbot to adults “until it can offer a safe, developmentally appropriate experience.” OpenAI said the group’s testing doesn’t reflect how the chatbot’s safeguards work. Parents, educators and child development experts have been sounding alarms over children’s use of AI chatbots, which have been blamed for facilitating cheating on schoolwork and even suicide. While even adults can fall victim to anthropomorphizing AI and develop unhealthy relationships with it, teenagers’ brains are not yet fully developed and they can be particularly vulnerable, child development experts say. “We are concerned that ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails that frequently don’t work,” said the report from Common Sense Media, a group that advocates for using digital media sensibly. Its report said that some teen-mode features worked as intended, including the chatbot’s refusal of explicit sexual role-play. Others that did not work as intended included alerts meant to notify parents if their child is at risk for suicide, self-harm or eating disorders, along with support for teens in crisis, Common Sense Media said. “ChatGPT still talks like a friend when teens treat it like a person,” the group said, though OpenAI had promised that the chatbot is prevented from suggesting it has personal feelings toward the user or implying that it is conscious or experiences emotions. OpenAI said it is “deeply committed to teen safety,” to developing safeguards and giving parents tools to guide their teens’ use of AI. The San Francisco company said its review of the report’s methodology shows “the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete, making their findings inaccurate.” Common Sense Media receives funding from OpenAI and other tech companies, including those whose services it evaluates.

headlines.title: Man sentenced to 50-years-to life for Mountain View cop shooting
headlines.description: A Union City man was sentenced to 50-years-to life in prison Wednesday for the attempted murder of a Mountain View police officer, the Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office said. Jeffrey Choy, 43, shot officer Brian Buckelew on July 16, 2022, during a traffic stop, prosecutors said. Buckelew was shot at an arm’s length away; he recovered from his injuries and has returned to his job. The officer was conducting DUI enforcement and pulled Choy over after midnight after he saw him run a stop sign near Villa and Hope streets in Mountain View. Choy then drove through a four-way intersection. When Buckelew approached the driver’s side of Choy’s car, the two exchanged greetings before Choy raised a 9mm handgun and fired it twice. One bullet missed the officer and the other went through is arm and struck his bullet-proof vest. After the shooting, Choy took off and then crashed his car near Higdon Avenue, where he got out and fled on foot. He hid in a laundry room and then left the city. Police caught up to Choy at a Black Bear Diner in Fremont the next day, where he was having brunch with his family. Choy, a felon, was barred from having any weapons. At the time of the shooting, he was out on bail but had an active warrant for being in possession of a gun during a March 2022 traffic stop.

headlines.title: Golden Gate Bridge drivers face back-to-back lane closures
headlines.description: Golden Gate Bridge drivers should expect delays Thursday as crews wrap up midday roadway maintenance before returning for overnight seismic retrofit work. The midday lane closures begin at 9:30 a.m., with the bridge scheduled to reopen by 2 p.m. The work is part of a weeklong series of closures, with the next round scheduled for Nov. 2 to 5. Then at 9 p.m., crews will close some lanes for seismic retrofit construction. Both northbound and southbound traffic will remain open during the overnight work, but delays are possible. The bridge is expected to return to its normal configuration by 5 a.m. Overnight work will continue later in the day.

headlines.title: Burton's 3-pointer with 41 seconds left helps send Valkyries past Aces 83-81 for 2-0 semifinals lead
headlines.description: Veronica Burton hit a deep 3-pointer that put Golden State ahead with 41 seconds left and converted two free throws in the closing seconds, Tiffany Hayes had 21 points, and the Valkyries held off the Las Vegas Aces 83-81 on Wednesday night for a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five WNBA semifinal series. In a wild finish, Jackie Young missed the second of two free throws with six seconds left to give Las Vegas one last chance and Chelsea Gray grabbed the rebound and droved under the basket for a layup attempt. Kiah Stokes blocked the shot and Burton corralled the ball. Gabby Williams had 20 points and five rebounds and Kayla Thornton scored 16 points as the Valkyries moved one win away from reaching the WNBA Finals in just their second season. Golden State became the first expansion team in league history to make the playoffs in its inaugural season last year. A shot-clock violation gave Golden State the ball back with 1:01 to play and Burton delivered with her lone basket of the night. The series now shifts to Las Vegas for Game 3 on Friday with the defending champions trying to stave off elimination. Coach Becky Hammon said before Wednesday’s game how important it would be to go home with a split — but the Valkyries have been too good in front of their rocking home crowd and now Hammon’s team is on the brink of the season ending without a repeat title. A’ja Wilson had 24 points on 9-for-16 shooting and seven rebounds for Las Vegas, which trailed 66-55 going into the final 10 minutes and made it interesting down the stretch. Gray’s jumper with 4:46 to go pulled the Aces to 73-68 then Dana Evans’ 3-pointer made it 74-71 before Gray hit a tying 3 with 2:10 left. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

headlines.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026: Events, schedules, what to know
headlines.description: It’s that time of year again. San Francisco Fleet Week is back. The fall tradition will be highlighted by the Blue Angels screaming across the skies, but there are plenty of other events to experience. Check out the guide below to learn more about Fleet Week events. What is San Francisco Fleet Week? San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual celebration of the nation’s sea services. A multi-day air show, parade of ships and ship tours highlight the weeklong festivities. “San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual public event that honors the contributions of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces while advancing cooperation and knowledge among civilian- and military-based Humanitarian Assistance personnel,” a statement on the event’s website reads. When is San Francisco Fleet Week 2026? Fleet Week is scheduled to take place Sunday, Oct. 4 through Monday, Oct. 12. San Francisco Fleet Week Air Show Head to a location along San Francisco Bay between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz to catch a thrilling aerial show featuring the Blue Angels, a United Airlines 777, and much more.
